雋也平原君俠客之雄也公孫弘曲學之
陋也而亦儒耶雖荀卿賈誼劉向揚雄之
所稱述尚猶時不能無抵捂以入於儒為
punctuated:
於議官，農出於農稷之官，小說出於稗官，則不能無可疑者。夫自周之衰，官失其守，百家自伸其說，果何所總統哉？固之臆說，恐未足以得其原也。
且夫儒之道大矣！三才之所以立，萬民之所以治，六經之所以同歸於道也；二帝三王、周公、孔子之所以垂心法而立極也，而孰能小之？固之言曰：「惑者既失精微，而辟者又離道本，是以五經乖離，儒學寖衰。」夫其所謂患，乃惑與辟者之救也，非儒之道固然也。因其惑與辟者之救儒也，而儕儒與九流列，不得與六藝同科，尚為知儒者乎？
就其所謂儒者而校之，孟氏純乎純，六經之翼也；曾子、子思、漆雕、宓子之書，雖後人所輯，亦孔門之遺焉。乃若晏子，伯佐之流也；魯仲連，策士之雋也；平原君，俠客之雄也；公孫弘，曲學之陋也，而亦儒耶？雖荀卿、賈誼、劉向、揚雄之所稱述，尚猶時不能無牴牾，以入於儒焉
translation_en:
…from deliberative officials, the Agriculturalists from officials responsible for agriculture and grain, and the Minor Tales school from petty officials: these claims cannot be free from doubt. From the decline of the Zhou onward, officials failed to maintain their proper duties, and the hundred schools each advanced their own doctrines. What, indeed, could have exercised overall direction over them? Ban Gu’s conjectures, I fear, are insufficient to establish their origins.
Moreover, how great is the Way of the Confucians! It is that by which the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—are established, the myriad people are governed, and the Six Classics converge upon the Way. It is that by which the Two Emperors, the Three Kings, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius handed down the teaching of the mind and established the supreme standard. Who could diminish it? Ban Gu says: “The deluded have already lost its subtle essence, while the deviant have departed from the root of the Way. Thus the Five Classics have become disjoined, and Confucian learning has gradually declined.” Yet the trouble of which he speaks is the fault [?] of the deluded and deviant; it is not inherent in the Confucian Way. Because of the harm [?] these deluded and deviant people have done to Confucian learning, he ranks the Confucians alongside the Nine Schools, denying them the same standing as the Six Arts. Can he still be called someone who understands Confucian learning?
Let us examine those whom he calls Confucians. Master Meng is purity itself, an aid to the Six Classics. The books of Zengzi, Zisi, Qidiao, and Mizi, although compiled by later people, likewise preserve a legacy of Confucius’s school. But Yanzi belongs among assistants to hegemons; Lu Zhonglian was an outstanding political strategist; the Lord of Pingyuan was a mighty figure among knights-errant; and Gongsun Hong exemplified the baseness of twisting learning to suit circumstances. Were these also Confucians? Even the writings and teachings of Xun Qing, Jia Yi, Liu Xiang, and Yang Xiong could not always avoid contradictions; as for their inclusion among the Confucians…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
未全况其他乎而胡為乎數子之與儒列
也夫其以數子者為儒則其儕儒以列於
九流不足異矣盖其說原於司馬談氏論
陰陽儒墨名法道德六家之要而曰儒者
博而寡要勞而少功宜不免於後六經之
譏矣而惜乎固之復淺於知儒也孔子曰
今衆人之命儒也妄常以儒相詬病非是
之謂耶若夫舍儒而論各家則其本指已
不能無救非如儒者之救於末流矣而君
===
子胡可以弗擇也彼翕張與奪縱橫之所
從出也遣去情累名法之所從出也此蘇
張申韓所以亂天下而禍後世雖本原於
道德之說然其害烈矣固無所擇而皆取
之後世何稽焉乃若十家之不取小說則
以稗言無益乎政理黜之盖無足論也而
愚獨竊有感焉夫以諸葛孔明之賢而尚
申韓以佐治溺霸術之餘流矣以韓愈之
智而言孔墨必相為用蹈文人之迷轍矣

也夫其以數子者爲儒則其儕儒以列於

陰陽儒墨名法道德六家之要而曰儒者
愽而寡要勞而少功宜不免於後六經之

===
子胡可以弗擇也彼翕張與奪縱横之所
從出也遣去情累名法之所從出也此蘇

申韓以佐治溺霸術之餘流矣以韓愈之
智而言孔墨必相爲用蹈文人之迷繳矣
punctuated:
未全，况其他乎？而胡為乎數子之與儒列也？夫其以數子者為儒，則其儕儒以列於九流，不足異矣。盖其說原於司馬談氏論陰陽、儒、墨、名、法、道德六家之要，而曰：「儒者博而寡要，勞而少功。」宜不免於後六經之譏矣。而惜乎固之復淺於知儒也！孔子曰：「今衆人之命儒也妄，常以儒相詬病。」非是之謂耶？若夫舍儒而論各家，則其本指已不能無救，非如儒者之救於末流矣。而君子胡可以弗擇也？彼翕張與奪，縱橫之所從出也；遣去情累，名法之所從出也。此蘇張申韓所以亂天下而禍後世，雖本原於道德之說，然其害烈矣。固無所擇而皆取之，後世何稽焉？乃若十家之不取小說，則以稗言無益乎政理黜之，盖無足論也。
而愚獨竊有感焉。夫以諸葛孔明之賢，而尚申韓以佐治，溺霸術之餘流矣；以韓愈之智，而言孔墨必相為用，蹈文人之迷轍矣。
translation_en:
…their inclusion among the Confucians is not wholly warranted; how much less that of the others? Why, then, are these men ranked among the Confucians? If he regards these men as Confucians, it is hardly surprising that he also places the Confucians alongside the other schools among the Nine Currents. His account derives from Sima Tan’s discussion of the essentials of the six schools—Yin-Yang, Confucian, Mohist, Names, Legalist, and the Way and Its Power—in which he says: “The Confucians are broad in learning but seldom grasp the essentials; they labor much but accomplish little.” He surely cannot escape the criticism that he relegates the Six Classics to a subordinate position. How regrettable that Ban Gu, too, should have so shallow an understanding of the Confucians! Confucius said: “Nowadays people apply the name ‘Confucian’ indiscriminately, constantly using it to revile one another.” Is this not precisely what he meant?
If we set the Confucians aside and discuss the other schools, their very foundational principles already require correction. This differs from Confucian teaching, where correction is needed only in its later derivative forms. How, then, can the gentleman fail to discriminate? Contraction and expansion, giving and taking: these are the source of the teachings of the diplomatic strategists. Dispelling emotional entanglements: this is the source of the teachings of Names and Laws. These were the means by which Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei threw the world into disorder and brought calamity upon later generations. Though rooted in teachings concerning the Way and Its Power, their harm was grievous. Ban Gu makes no distinctions but accepts them all: what standard can later generations find in him? As for his exclusion of the school of minor tales from the Ten Schools, he rejects it because its petty accounts contribute nothing to government and good order. This scarcely merits discussion.
Yet I, in my humble view, find particular cause for reflection here. Worthy though Zhuge Kongming was, he esteemed Shen Buhai and Han Fei as aids to government, becoming submerged in the lingering currents of the techniques of hegemony. Wise though Han Yu was, he declared that the teachings of Confucius and Mozi must serve one another’s purposes, thus following the misguided tracks of literary men.

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
蘇洵謂諫者以蘇張之機智勇辨濟其忠
權謀之偏說乎蘇軾謂聖人莊周所推尊
特陽擠而陰助之譎辨之游辭乎儒者宜
峻其防以障之尚可揚波而助瀾也哉夫
理術不明士惑於所從嚮以數子高世之
識其取舎尚如是他亦何議焉故君子之
學不可不慎所擇也雖然此特就歆固所
志言也漢史而後舊籍多逸聞風而作者
益繁盖非四庫崇文之所能載經生學士
===
窮年皓首卒不能殫其說矣于何而擇之
曰致力於六經則其本立矣執六經以契
勘諸子如鑑之照物而妍媸畢陳雖泛濫
於百家不足為吾惑而且將為吾用所謂
取之博歸之約盖庶幾矣若於此競多以
闘靡秘竒以助談譁眾以取稱則多聞見
而岐於他道君子之所闢也尚足以為學
乎抑儒之厄于異論豈特漢世然哉隋唐
而下其不知儒猶昔也有宋真儒輩出摧

translation_en:
Su Xun said that a remonstrant should supplement his loyalty with the resourcefulness, intelligence, courage, and eloquence of Su Qin and Zhang Yi. Is this not a one-sided doctrine of expedient scheming? Su Shi said that the sages were those whom Zhuang Zhou revered, and that he merely attacked them openly while supporting them covertly. Is this not the evasive language of specious argument? Confucian scholars should strengthen their defenses to block such doctrines. How could they instead stir up the waves and swell the surge? When principles and methods are unclear, scholars become confused about which direction to follow. If even these men, whose discernment surpassed their age, made such choices about what to accept and reject, what need is there to discuss others? Thus, in his learning, the gentleman must be careful about what he chooses.

Yet this discussion concerns only what Liu Xin and Ban Gu recorded. After the History of the Han, many old writings were lost, while authors inspired to follow earlier examples became ever more numerous. Their works surely exceeded what the Four Repositories and the Chongwen Catalogue could contain. Students of the classics and learned scholars could spend all their years studying until their hair turned white and still fail to exhaust these teachings. On what basis, then, should one choose? I say: devote yourself to the Six Classics, and your foundation will be established. Use the Six Classics to examine and verify the various masters, just as a mirror reflects objects and reveals both beauty and ugliness. Though I range widely through the hundred schools, they will not confuse me; indeed, they will become useful to me. This comes close to what is meant by drawing broadly upon learning and bringing it back to essentials.

But if one competes in the quantity of one's learning to vie in ornate display, treasures rarities to embellish conversation, and courts the crowd to win acclaim, then one's extensive learning and experience lead one astray onto other paths. This is what the gentleman rejects. Can it still count as learning? Moreover, was the distress inflicted on Confucian learning by divergent doctrines confined to the Han? From the Sui and Tang onward, people remained as ignorant of Confucian learning as before. In the Song, true Confucian scholars arose in succession, breaking down…

text:

translation_en:
…broke through and cleared away opposition. Only then did the Confucians of later ages cease to be ranked alongside the Hundred Schools. Regrettably, the rulers of the time still could not employ Confucians. Our successive sage emperors alone have continued the essential teachings of the ancient emperors and kings, thereby bringing about pure and harmonious government, wholeheartedly selecting Confucians for service. Thus scholars discuss nothing outside Confucian learning, and officials act only according to Confucian principles. title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
務而慎所決擇其士之俊傑者耶
考試官大學士李批學以達事變為難于能舉
唐宋諸臣變法不善而極論之使人知朝廷興衰之
故瞭然可為後世之明鑒也佳士佳士
法之善者所必守而不善守者則適以決
天下之防法之弊者所必變而不善變者
則適以滋天下之擾自昔帝王之興更事
多而備患密其所創法未有不善間有迫
于相沿之勢取一切之權不暇為萬世計
===
者則在後人隨時消息去其太甚變而不
輕變斯無負于謀國耳法當守而不守則
為紛更當變而不變則為裕蠱變之不至
于紛更則積蠹去而先王之法益修守之
不至于裕蠱則舊章存而先王之業益固
唐宋諸臣胥失之豈非千載之鑒戒哉試
為執事誦所聞夫天下之事非一身一家
之事也君子之臨事謀之而當則天下後
世與其福謀之而不當則天下後世與其

punctuated:
務而慎所決擇，其士之俊傑者耶？
考試官大學士李批：學以達事變為難，于能舉唐宋諸臣變法不善而極論之，使人知朝廷興衰之故，瞭然可為後世之明鑒也。佳士！佳士！
法之善者所必守，而不善守者則適以決天下之防；法之弊者所必變，而不善變者則適以滋天下之擾。自昔帝王之興，更事多而備患密，其所創法未有不善。間有迫于相沿之勢，取一切之權，不暇為萬世計者，則在後人隨時消息，去其太甚，變而不輕變，斯無負于謀國耳。法當守而不守，則為紛更；當變而不變，則為裕蠱。變之不至于紛更，則積蠹去而先王之法益修；守之不至于裕蠱，則舊章存而先王之業益固。唐宋諸臣胥失之，豈非千載之鑒戒哉？試為執事誦所聞。夫天下之事，非一身一家之事也。君子之臨事，謀之而當，則天下後世與其福；謀之而不當，則天下後世與其
translation_en:
…affairs, and exercises care in making decisions: is he not an outstanding scholar?
Examiner Li, Grand Secretary, comments: The difficulty in learning lies in comprehending changing affairs. The candidate [?] can cite the ill-advised reforms of Tang and Song ministers and discuss them thoroughly, enabling readers to understand the causes of a dynasty’s rise and decline. His account clearly provides an illuminating mirror for later generations. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!
Good laws must be preserved; yet those who preserve them poorly merely breach the realm’s defenses. Defective laws must be changed; yet those who change them poorly merely increase disturbances throughout the realm. From antiquity, when emperors and kings rose to power, they had experienced many affairs and made thorough provision against calamity; none of the laws they established was without merit. Occasionally, however, the force of inherited circumstances compelled them to adopt temporary expedients, leaving no leisure to plan for all future ages. It then falls to their successors to adjust matters to the times and remove the worst excesses—to make changes without changing things lightly. Only thus can they fulfill their responsibility for planning the affairs of state. Failing to preserve laws that ought to be preserved amounts to disruptive alteration; failing to change those that ought to be changed amounts to fostering decay. If change stops short of disruptive alteration, accumulated abuses are removed and the laws of the former kings are further perfected. If preservation stops short of fostering decay, established institutions survive and the foundations laid by the former kings become firmer still. The ministers of the Tang and Song all failed in this respect. Is this not a warning for a thousand years? Allow me to recount for you, honored examiners, what I have learned. The affairs of the realm are not the affairs of a single person or family. When a gentleman confronts affairs and plans appropriately, the whole realm and later generations share in the blessings; if his planning is inappropriate, the whole realm and later generations share in his…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
憂是故立心欲遠而慮事欲周集議欲虛
而當幾欲斷國有大議而取决于吾之一
言固有利干近而貽萬世之害亦有害于
近而實萬世之利者固有出于芻蕘而其
言可取亦有出于卿士而其言可棄者非
君子有見幾之哲廓虛受之公則亦孰能
决而用之也唐宋以來守圉之臣則患無
兵團結召募日以益兵為議然兵益則國
儲難給兵不可以輕益也司計之臣則患
===
無財頭會箕斂日以加賦為事然賦加則
民力難堪賦不可以輕加也曷不求其初
而斟酌損益以善其後乎唐初府衛之制
盖沿周隋之舊統以折衝果毅而隷之十
六衛以教閱則有期以番上則有期兵行
則發以符契兵休則散歸田畝國家無聚
兵之費而將帥無擅兵之患三代以降盖
兵制之最善者陸贄稱其有居重馭輕之
權而不至于倒持有昭德蓄威之畧而不

而斟酌損益以善其後乎唐初府衛之制

punctuated: 憂。是故立心欲遠，而慮事欲周；集議欲虛，而當幾欲斷。國有大議，而取决于吾之一言，固有利干近而貽萬世之害，亦有害于近而實萬世之利者；固有出于芻蕘而其言可取，亦有出于卿士而其言可棄者。非君子有見幾之哲、廓虛受之公，則亦孰能决而用之也？唐宋以來，守圉之臣則患無兵，團結召募，日以益兵為議。然兵益則國儲難給，兵不可以輕益也。司計之臣則患無財，頭會箕斂，日以加賦為事。然賦加則民力難堪，賦不可以輕加也。曷不求其初，而斟酌損益，以善其後乎？唐初府衛之制，盖沿周隋之舊，統以折衝果毅，而隷之十六衛。以教閱則有期，以番上則有期。兵行則發以符契，兵休則散歸田畝。國家無聚兵之費，而將帥無擅兵之患。三代以降，盖兵制之最善者。陸贄稱其有居重馭輕之權而不至于倒持，有昭德蓄威之畧而不
translation_en:
…share in its sorrows. Thus one’s purposes should be far-reaching and one’s deliberations comprehensive; in gathering opinions one should be receptive, and at the critical moment decisive. When the state faces a great question and the decision rests upon a single word from us, some measures offer immediate advantage [?] yet leave harm for ten thousand generations, while others cause immediate harm yet truly benefit ten thousand generations. Some proposals come from grass-cutters and wood-gatherers yet deserve acceptance; others come from high ministers and officers yet deserve rejection. Unless a gentleman possesses the wisdom to discern the first signs of change and the impartiality to receive others’ views with an open mind, who can decide among them and put them into practice?

Since the Tang and Song, officials defending the frontiers have worried about shortages of troops. Organizing units and recruiting men, they have continually advocated increasing troop numbers. Yet when troops increase, state reserves cannot readily supply them: troops must not be increased lightly. Officials managing finance have worried about shortages of funds. Levying by the head and gathering taxes by the basketful, they have continually made increasing taxation their business. Yet when taxes increase, the people’s resources cannot bear the burden: taxes must not be increased lightly. Why not investigate the original arrangements and weigh what should be reduced or increased, so as to improve subsequent conditions?

The system of military prefectures and guards in the early Tang generally followed the precedents of the Zhou and Sui. Troops were commanded by Intrepid and Resolute Commandants and assigned to the Sixteen Guards. Training and inspection took place at prescribed times, as did service at the capital in rotation. When troops went on campaign, they were mobilized by tallies; when military service ceased, they dispersed and returned to their fields. The state incurred no expense for maintaining concentrated troops, and there was no danger of commanders exercising unauthorized control over them. Of the military systems since the Three Dynasties, this was surely the best. Lu Zhi praised it for possessing the means to control the lesser forces through a strong center without allowing authority to be inverted, and for possessing a strategy of manifesting virtue and building up military might without…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
至于偏廢信太宗之訏謨也迨至開元郎
將之遞遷不以時衛士之番上不以時士
多逃匿而府兵之制隳矣張說廼變為彍
騎之法募同華諸州兵卒以實之然士不
土着鮮有固志無事則寄名尺籍兾沾糧
賜有事則竄身山澤各思自免安史之變
衛士不能受甲則何以威不軌而壯國勢
乎此張說之變府兵所以為唐之厲階也
宋初懲藩鎮跋扈盡收天下勁兵聚之京
===
師雖一時得强幹弱支之術而聚兵之多
已不可散延及治平兵之隸籍者百十六
萬天下之困于兵未有如宋者矣故安石
建議變之其意盖欲去冗兵以省國計豈
可盡非也然所創保甲于國無捍禦之益
于民有侵擾之害卒之鄉兵既不可用而
募兵不可復省是于唐人府兵之意猶未
之得也况周官田賦之制乎此宋之兵制
可變而安石不善變則重以困天下之力

之得也況周官田賦之制乎此宋之兵制
可變而安石不善變則重以困天下之力
punctuated:
至于偏廢，信太宗之訏謨也。迨至開元，郎將之遞遷不以時，衛士之番上不以時，士多逃匿，而府兵之制隳矣。張說廼變為彍騎之法，募同華諸州兵卒以實之。然士不土着，鮮有固志，無事則寄名尺籍，兾沾糧賜；有事則竄身山澤，各思自免。安史之變，衛士不能受甲，則何以威不軌而壯國勢乎？此張說之變府兵，所以為唐之厲階也。
宋初懲藩鎮跋扈，盡收天下勁兵，聚之京師。雖一時得强幹弱支之術，而聚兵之多，已不可散。延及治平，兵之隸籍者百十六萬。天下之困于兵，未有如宋者矣。故安石建議變之，其意盖欲去冗兵以省國計，豈可盡非也？然所創保甲，于國無捍禦之益，于民有侵擾之害。卒之鄉兵既不可用，而募兵不可復省，是于唐人府兵之意猶未之得也，况周官田賦之制乎？此宋之兵制可變，而安石不善變，則重以困天下之力
translation_en:
…result in neglect of either aspect: this was indeed Emperor Taizong’s grand design. By the Kaiyuan era, however, the rotation and transfer of military officers (langjiang) no longer took place at the proper times, nor did the guardsmen’s tours of duty at the capital. Many soldiers fled or went into hiding, and the fubing militia system fell into ruin. Zhang Yue then replaced it with the Guoqi cavalry system, recruiting soldiers from Tongzhou, Huazhou, and other prefectures to fill its ranks. Yet these soldiers had no local roots, and few possessed steadfast resolve. In peaceful times they entered their names on the military rolls in hopes of receiving grain allowances and rewards; when trouble arose, they fled into the mountains and marshes, each seeking his own escape. During the An Lushan–Shi Siming rebellion, the guardsmen could not even take up arms. How, then, could they overawe rebels and strengthen the state? This is why Zhang Yue’s transformation of the fubing system became a source of calamity for the Tang.
At the beginning of the Song, taking warning from the insubordination of the regional military governors, the dynasty gathered all the realm’s elite troops in the capital. Although this temporarily achieved the aim of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, the troops assembled were already too numerous to disperse. By the Zhiping era, those on the military rolls numbered 1,160,000. Never had the realm been so burdened by its army as under the Song. Thus Wang Anshi proposed reform. His intention was presumably to eliminate superfluous troops and reduce state expenditure; how could it be condemned outright? Yet the baojia household militia system he established brought the state no benefit in defense and subjected the people to harassment. In the end, the local militia proved unusable, while the recruited troops could no longer be reduced. He had thus failed even to grasp the intent of the Tang fubing system, much less the system of land-based military levies in the Offices of Zhou! The Song military system therefore warranted reform, but Anshi did not reform it well, thereby placing a still heavier burden on the resources of the realm…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
矣唐初租庸調之制盖沿元魏之舊授之
以口分世業而徵之以丁身有田則有租
有身則有庸有家則有調輸入則有常而
不責所無灾傷則有免而遞減其數國家
得均田之法而四境多敦本之民三代以
降盖經制之最善者陸贄謂其域民也固
其取民也節信太宗之良法也天寶以後
則恒業廢于板蕩豪吏峻于誅求號稱白
着而租庸調之法亡矣楊炎廼變為兩稅
===
之法取大曆歲入最多者為額而征之然
時當蠱壞事出權宜戶以見居為簿則逃
民無倖免人以貧富為差則困窮無重累
但舎所有之粟帛責民以所無之錢貨輕
錢重遂為民後日之患攤稅之弊邑里日
至空虛則何以恤人窮而裕國計乎此楊
炎之兩稅雖變唐之賦法而功罪猶相半
者也宋初制諸鎮以執其財用之權而緩
急歛散盈縮悉歸三司雖去一時尾大不

唐初租庸調之制，盖沿元魏之舊，授之以口分世業，而徵之以丁身。有田則有租，有身則有庸，有家則有調。輸入則有常，而不責所無；灾傷則有免，而遞減其數。國家得均田之法，而四境多敦本之民。三代以降，盖經制之最善者。陸贄謂其域民也固，其取民也節，信太宗之良法也。天寶以後，則恒業廢于板蕩，豪吏峻于誅求，號稱白着，而租庸調之法亡矣。楊炎廼變為兩稅之法，取大曆歲入最多者為額而征之。然時當蠱壞，事出權宜，戶以見居為簿，則逃民無倖免；人以貧富為差，則困窮無重累。但舎所有之粟帛，責民以所無之錢，貨輕錢重，遂為民後日之患。攤稅之弊，邑里日至空虛，則何以恤人窮而裕國計乎？此楊炎之兩稅，雖變唐之賦法，而功罪猶相半者也。

宋初制諸鎮，以執其財用之權，而緩急歛散盈縮悉歸三司，雖去一時尾大不
translation_en:
…indeed.

The early Tang system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and household levy largely followed the old arrangements of the Northern Wei. People were granted land allotted per person and land held in hereditary tenure, while levies were assessed on adult males. Possession of land entailed the grain tax; being an adult male entailed labor service; having a household entailed the household levy. Payments were fixed, and people were not required to supply what they lacked. When disasters caused losses, exemptions were granted and the amounts progressively reduced. The state secured a method of equalizing land allotments, and throughout the realm many people devoted themselves to agriculture, the fundamental occupation. Of the institutional arrangements since the Three Dynasties, this was probably the best. Lu Zhi said that it firmly settled the people and took from them with restraint. It was indeed an excellent system of Emperor Taizong.

After the Tianbao era, however, permanent holdings were destroyed amid turmoil, and overbearing officials became harsh in their exactions, which were called baizhuo, “unwarranted levies” [?]. The system of grain tax, labor service, and household levy thus disappeared. Yang Yan then replaced it with the twice-yearly tax system, setting the revenue quota at the highest annual receipts of the Dali era and collecting accordingly. Yet this was a time of deterioration, and the measure arose as an expedient. Registering households where they currently resided meant that fugitives could not escape taxation by good fortune; grading people according to their wealth meant that the destitute were not heavily burdened. But it disregarded the grain and silk they possessed and demanded the cash they lacked. Goods became cheap and money dear, bringing subsequent hardship upon the people. Through the abuses of redistributing tax liabilities, towns and villages grew emptier by the day. How could this relieve the people's poverty and provide ample resources for the state? Thus, although Yang Yan's twice-yearly tax changed the Tang system of taxation, its merits and faults remained evenly balanced.

At the beginning of the Song, the court brought the regional military commands under control in order to take charge of their finances. Whether expenditures were deferrable or urgent, revenues collected or disbursed, and funds in surplus or shortfall—all came under the Finance Commission. Although this removed the immediate danger of a tail too large to…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
掉之患而郊賚兵餉財之取于民者已不
可加中更契丹元昊之變歲費之隸會計
者踰一億萬天下之困于財未有如宋者
矣故安石建議更之其意蓋欲豐國儲以
張武功豈可過責也然所創條例更累朝
常平之舊急編氓青苗之息卒之侵疆未
復而邦本已摇是雖壽昌斂散之法猶未
之得也况周官均節之式乎此宋之經制
可變而安石不善變則重以竭天下之財
===
矣唐之名臣若李泌嘗議復府兵矣陸贄
嘗議復租庸調矣而議之不行非舊法之
不可復也欲復租庸調則先復府兵府兵
既復則民安其口分世業而租庸調始可
復耳唐至肅代則天下日多故矣而二公
又不得乆于其位如之何舊法之可復也
君子于是深罪乎張說也使張說善守府
兵之制則内兵足以制方鎮而安史之亂
不生矣又何至于極壞而賦入之常皆不

掉之患，而郊賚兵餉，財之取于民者已不可加。中更契丹、元昊之變，歲費之隸會計者踰一億萬，天下之困于財，未有如宋者矣。故安石建議更之，其意蓋欲豐國儲以張武功，豈可過責也？然所創條例，更累朝常平之舊，急編氓青苗之息，卒之侵疆未復，而邦本已摇。是雖壽昌斂散之法猶未之得也，况《周官》均節之式乎？此宋之經制可變，而安石不善變，則重以竭天下之財矣。
唐之名臣若李泌，嘗議復府兵矣；陸贄，嘗議復租庸調矣。而議之不行，非舊法之不可復也。欲復租庸調，則先復府兵；府兵既復，則民安其口分、世業，而租庸調始可復耳。唐至肅、代，則天下日多故矣，而二公又不得乆于其位，如之何舊法之可復也？君子于是深罪乎張說也。使張說善守府兵之制，則内兵足以制方鎮，而安史之亂不生矣。又何至于極壞，而賦入之常皆不
translation_en:
…the danger of an overgrown tail that could no longer be moved. Yet gifts bestowed at the suburban sacrifices and soldiers’ pay already made it impossible to increase further the wealth extracted from the people. Subsequently came the crises involving the Khitan and Yuanhao, and annual expenditure entered in the fiscal accounts exceeded a hundred million [?]. Never had the realm suffered financial distress like that under the Song. Thus Anshi proposed reforms. His intention was presumably to replenish the state’s reserves so as to expand its military achievements; how could one blame him excessively? Yet the regulations he introduced altered the ever-normal granary practices inherited from successive reigns and pressed the registered commoners for interest on Green Sprouts loans. In the end, the territory seized by invaders remained unrecovered, while the foundations of the state had already been shaken. He had not even grasped Shouchang’s methods of collecting and distributing grain, much less the principles of equitable allocation and restraint in expenditure set out in the Offices of Zhou! Thus the Song’s established institutions could indeed be changed, but Anshi’s inept changes only further exhausted the realm’s wealth.
Among the Tang’s eminent ministers, Li Mi once proposed restoring the militia system, and Lu Zhi once proposed restoring the grain tax, labor-service commutation, and household levy. Their proposals went unimplemented, but this was not because the old institutions could not be restored. To restore those taxes, one first had to restore the militia system. Once that system was restored, the people could securely occupy their allotted and hereditary fields, and only then could those taxes be restored. By the reigns of Suzong and Daizong, troubles throughout the realm were multiplying daily; moreover, these two gentlemen could not remain long in office. How, then, could the old institutions have been restored? On this account, the gentleman lays grave blame upon Zhang Yue. Had Zhang Yue properly preserved the militia system, the troops of the central government would have sufficed to control the regional military commands, and the An–Shi Rebellion would never have arisen. How, then, could matters have reached such utter ruin that even the regular arrangements for tax revenue could no longer…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
能守其故乎宋之名臣若司馬光盖嘗欲
免保甲矣蠲除條例矣而不久復行非新
法之不可去也欲革熈寧之失政當先釐
治平之積蠹積蠹既除則治軍省賦皆可
舉行而新法之不善者始可去耳宋至元
祐則小人日結黨以伺隙矣而君實盡去
其法雖助役之善不少遺使紹聖借為口
實君實與公著諸賢復相繼不祿則如之
何新法之不復行也君子于是深罪乎安
===
石也使安石善變募兵之制則新兵足以
任戍守而經制之錢可省矣又何急於豐
財使章蔡之徒復藉口以播惡乎嗟夫天
下之事未易言也好學如安石得君如安
石而神宗復以大有為之君聽斷于上君
臣相期思以革天下之弊而與民更始志
非不壮夷考其終廼志勤功鮮曾不及慶
曆諸賢此謀國之所以難也然安石欲建
富强之業而勞擾若此則亦不考宋初之

何新法之不復行也君子于是深罪乎安
===

任戍守而經制之錢可省矣又何急於豐

石而神宗復以大有為之君聽斷于上君

非不壮矣考其終迴志勤功鮮曾不及慶
曆諸賢比謀國之所以難也然安石欲建
富强之業而勞擾若此則亦不考宋初之
punctuated:
能守其故乎？宋之名臣若司馬光，盖嘗欲免保甲矣，蠲除條例矣，而不久復行，非新法之不可去也。欲革熈寧之失政，當先釐治平之積蠹。積蠹既除，則治軍省賦皆可舉行，而新法之不善者始可去耳。宋至元祐，則小人日結黨以伺隙矣，而君實盡去其法，雖助役之善不少遺，使紹聖借為口實。君實與公著諸賢復相繼不祿，則如之何新法之不復行也？君子于是深罪乎安石也。使安石善變募兵之制，則新兵足以任戍守，而經制之錢可省矣，又何急於豐財，使章蔡之徒復藉口以播惡乎？

嗟夫！天下之事未易言也。好學如安石，得君如安石，而神宗復以大有為之君聽斷于上，君臣相期，思以革天下之弊，而與民更始，志非不壮。夷考其終，廼志勤功鮮，曾不及慶曆諸賢，此謀國之所以難也。然安石欲建富强之業，而勞擾若此，則亦不考宋初之
translation_en:
…retain their former arrangements? Among the celebrated ministers of the Song, Sima Guang sought to abolish the baojia system of household organization and repeal the regulations, yet before long they were put into effect again. This was not because the New Policies could not be removed. To remedy the misgovernment of the Xining era, one first had to clear away the abuses accumulated during the Zhiping era. Once those entrenched abuses were eliminated, measures to put the army in order and reduce taxation could all be implemented; only then could the unsound elements of the New Policies be removed. By the Yuanyou era of the Song, petty men were increasingly forming factions and watching for an opening. Yet Junshi—that is, Sima Guang—abolished those policies entirely, retaining not even the beneficial provisions for contributions toward service obligations. This gave those in power during the Shaosheng era a pretext. Junshi, Gongzhu, and the other worthy men then died one after another: how, under these circumstances, could the New Policies fail to be restored? The gentleman therefore lays grave blame upon Anshi. Had Anshi properly reformed the system of recruiting soldiers, the new troops would have sufficed for garrison duty, and expenditure on the established military arrangements could have been reduced. Why, then, would there have been any urgency to increase revenues, giving the likes of Zhang and Cai another pretext for spreading harm?

Alas! The affairs of the realm are not easily pronounced upon. Anshi was devoted to learning and enjoyed his sovereign’s confidence; moreover, Shenzong presided over decisions as a ruler intent on great accomplishments. Sovereign and minister placed their hopes in one another, intending to reform the abuses of the realm and make a fresh beginning with the people. Their ambition was certainly grand. Yet, on sober examination of the outcome, their purpose was earnest but their achievements few: they did not even equal the worthy men of the Qingli era. This shows why planning for the state is so difficult. Yet Anshi sought to establish wealth and strength, only to cause such toil and disturbance; thus he too failed to examine the circumstances of the early Song…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
故矣宋初以兵定僭偽功臣多而兵不滿
三十萬則天下之所患者非兵少也宋初
內營府寺外給軍旅費最鉅所仰給者止
中原數路則天下之所患者非財少也兵
不患少亦精之而已矣選伉健汰老弱而
行伍皆勝兵倡勇敢程技藝而教閱皆實
政則雖如唐初之府兵出則戰勝入則食
足可也雖如藝祖之征伐四克一振治平
之不競可也而何取於保甲也財不患少
===
亦節之而已矣裁冗員而吏兵易祿約冗
費而品式易供則雖如唐初之租庸調取
之不盈用之不匱可也雖如藝祖之貫朽
粟陳一洗治平之耗蠹可也而何取於條
例也自是而郊賚可節歲幣可革自是而
幽燕可取靈夏可收漢唐之舊疆可復神
宗之付托可無負矣安石謀之而術則疎
君實正之而施則未究此君子所以太息
於宋事也彼司兵不思國鈞之難繼而啓

punctuated: 故矣。宋初以兵定僭偽，功臣多而兵不滿三十萬，則天下之所患者非兵少也。宋初內營府寺，外給軍旅，費最鉅，所仰給者止中原數路，則天下之所患者非財少也。兵不患少，亦精之而已矣。選伉健，汰老弱，而行伍皆勝兵；倡勇敢，程技藝，而教閱皆實政。則雖如唐初之府兵，出則戰勝，入則食足，可也；雖如藝祖之征伐四克，一振治平之不競，可也。而何取於保甲也？財不患少，亦節之而已矣。裁冗員而吏兵易祿，約冗費而品式易供，則雖如唐初之租庸調，取之不盈，用之不匱，可也；雖如藝祖之貫朽粟陳，一洗治平之耗蠹，可也。而何取於條例也？自是而郊賚可節，歲幣可革；自是而幽燕可取，靈夏可收，漢唐之舊疆可復，神宗之付托可無負矣。安石謀之而術則疎，君實正之而施則未究，此君子所以太息於宋事也。彼司兵不思國鈞之難繼，而啓
translation_en:
…the precedents of the early Song. At the beginning of the Song, military force subdued the usurping regimes. There were many meritorious commanders, yet the troops numbered fewer than three hundred thousand. Thus, what the realm had to fear was not a shortage of soldiers. In the early Song, government offices were built at home and armies supplied in the field. Expenditure was enormous, yet it depended for its supplies on only a few circuits of the Central Plain. Thus, what the realm had to fear was not a shortage of wealth. There is no need to fear having few soldiers: one need only make them effective. Select the strong and vigorous and discharge the old and weak, so that every man in the ranks is fit to bear arms; encourage courage and assess military skills, so that training and reviews all serve a practical purpose. Then one could emulate the early Tang militia system: victorious in battle when deployed, and adequately fed when at home. One could also emulate the founding Song emperor’s conquests, victorious on every side, and at one stroke rouse the country from the weakness of the Zhiping era. What need, then, for the baojia system of household organization? Nor need one fear having little wealth: one need only exercise restraint. Eliminate superfluous personnel, and officials and soldiers will be readily paid; reduce unnecessary expenditure, and prescribed requirements will be readily supplied. Then one could emulate the early Tang system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and cloth levy: collections would not be excessive, and resources for expenditure would not run short. One could also emulate the founding Song emperor’s abundance, when the strings of stored coins rotted and grain grew old in the granaries, and at one stroke sweep away the waste and depredations of the Zhiping era. What need, then, for the Regulations Office?

By these means, rewards bestowed at the suburban sacrifices could be reduced and annual payments to foreign states abolished. By these means, You and Yan could be taken, Ling and Xia recovered, the former territories of the Han and Tang restored, and Emperor Shenzong’s trust fulfilled. Anshi planned for this, but his methods were inadequate; Junshi corrected matters, but his measures were never fully carried through. This is why the gentleman sighs deeply over the affairs of the Song. Those responsible for military affairs gave no thought to the difficulty of sustaining the governance of the state, and initiated…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
于益兵誠司兵之過司計不思民力之難
供而務于加賦誠司計之過矣昔者聖人
作易觀蠱之象特繫之曰先甲三日後甲
三日盖愼之也夫時久承平法紀漸隳天
下之隙潜伏于中而一旦潰出此變法之
會而世道升降之幾也故聖人愼之思其
所始思其所終果有通變宜民之術則愼
慮而勇為之如其未也寧固守成法而不
敢輕議焉此大人經綸之業幹蠱用譽之
===
道也若唐之張說宋之安石盖兩失之矣
惟我
皇祖以神武革元命作為典則以貽萬世
成祖復敦篤而駿惠之兵制財賦載在職掌
會典者品式具備邇者胡虜倭夷日蠢蠢焉
肆其不逞之謀屯兵不足以禦寇常賦不
足以供軍當事諸臣每煩奏
請而不知所出愚則以為此時之弊非法之
弊也為今之計愼選將帥以扞衞于外而

請而不知所出愚則以為此時之弊非法之
弊也為今之計慎選將帥以扞衛于外而
punctuated:
于益兵，誠司兵之過；司計不思民力之難供，而務于加賦，誠司計之過矣。昔者聖人作易，觀蠱之象，特繫之曰：「先甲三日，後甲三日。」盖愼之也。夫時久承平，法紀漸隳，天下之隙潜伏于中，而一旦潰出，此變法之會，而世道升降之幾也。故聖人愼之，思其所始，思其所終，果有通變宜民之術，則愼慮而勇為之；如其未也，寧固守成法，而不敢輕議焉。此大人經綸之業，幹蠱用譽之道也。若唐之張說、宋之安石，盖兩失之矣。
惟我皇祖以神武革元命，作為典則，以貽萬世。成祖復敦篤而駿惠之。兵制財賦載在職掌、會典者，品式具備。邇者胡虜倭夷日蠢蠢焉，肆其不逞之謀，屯兵不足以禦寇，常賦不足以供軍，當事諸臣每煩奏請，而不知所出。愚則以為此時之弊，非法之弊也。為今之計，愼選將帥以扞衞于外，而
translation_en:
…toward increasing the troops: this was indeed the fault of those responsible for military affairs. Those responsible for finances, failing to consider how difficult it was for the people's resources to meet the demands, devoted themselves to increasing taxation: this was indeed their fault. In antiquity, when the sage composed the Book of Changes, he contemplated the image of Gu, “Decay,” and specifically appended these words: “Three days before the jia day; three days after the jia day.” This expressed his caution. When peace has long prevailed, laws and discipline gradually deteriorate; fissures in the realm lie hidden within and then suddenly burst open. This is the occasion for changing institutions, and the critical juncture at which the world's fortunes rise or fall. Thus the sage proceeded cautiously, considering how matters began and how they would end. If one truly possesses a method of adapting to change and benefiting the people, one should deliberate cautiously and act boldly. If one does not yet possess it, one should rather hold firmly to established institutions and not venture lightly to propose changes. This is the great man's work of ordering the realm, the way of “remedying decay and thereby earning praise.” Zhang Yue of the Tang and Anshi of the Song both failed in this respect.
Our August Progenitor, through his divine martial prowess, brought the Yuan mandate to an end and established statutes and standards to be handed down for myriad generations. Chengzu further consolidated them and followed them with great devotion. The military institutions and fiscal provisions recorded in the Responsibilities of Offices and the Collected Statutes are complete in their categories and prescribed forms. Recently, the northern barbarians and Japanese marauders have grown increasingly restive, giving free rein to their lawless designs. The garrison troops are insufficient to repel the raiders, and regular tax revenues are insufficient to support the armies. The ministers responsible repeatedly trouble the throne with memorials requesting authorization, yet do not know where to obtain the resources. In my humble view, these are defects of the present circumstances, not defects of the institutions. The course to pursue now is carefully to select generals and commanders to defend the realm externally, and …

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
總之于督府則軍政修而
國威伸盜賊必知畏而不敢窺慎選守令以
綏輯于内而總之于撫臣則徭役省而惠
澤流黎民必知徳而不忍貳兵制財賦有
非

總之于督府，則軍政修而國威伸，盜賊必知畏而不敢窺。慎選守令，以綏輯于内，而總之于撫臣，則徭役省而惠澤流，黎民必知徳而不忍貳。兵制財賦有非祖宗之舊者，則亦因其廢墜而修舉之耳，無庸輕議也。《書》曰：「我不敢不監于有夏，亦不敢不監于有殷。」唐宋之事，亦後世之永監也。狂瞽之見若此，惟執事教之。

第五問
袁隨

同考試官主事張批〔平倭重計，士子類亦〕〔有能攄其算者，獨此策灼見東南事勢，條析〕〔七議，隱括幾宜，俱存遠猷，經濟之才也。〕

同考試官檢討殷批〔論南北事勢，歷歷如〕〔見，而籌畫周悉，無不切中機宜。誠如所言，倭不足〕〔平矣。識時務者在俊傑，非子其誰耶？〕

考試官侍講學士尹批〔明悉倭計，若畫□□〕
translation_en:
…and place them under the overall command of the supreme commander's headquarters. Military administration will then be put in order and the state's might asserted; the bandits will surely learn fear and dare not contemplate an incursion. Carefully select prefects and magistrates to bring peace and order within, and place them under the overall direction of the grand coordinators. Corvée obligations will then diminish and beneficence spread; the common people will surely appreciate this kindness and be unwilling to waver in their allegiance. Where military institutions, finances, and taxation depart from the old arrangements of the imperial ancestors, simply restore and implement what has fallen into disuse. There is no need to propose changes lightly. The Book of Documents says: “I dare not fail to take warning from the Xia, nor dare I fail to take warning from the Yin.” The affairs of the Tang and Song likewise provide lasting warnings for later generations. Such are my rash and benighted views; I ask you, sir, to instruct me.

Fifth Question
Yuan Sui 袁隨

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Bureau Secretary: “Pacifying the Japanese raiders requires weighty strategic deliberation. Among the candidates there are indeed those able to set forth their calculations, but this policy essay alone clearly perceives the circumstances of the southeast. It analyzes seven proposals individually, encompassing the subtleties of timing and appropriate action, all with foresight. Here is a talent for statecraft.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Hanlin Compiler: “His discussion of circumstances in the south and north is so vivid that one seems to see them, and his planning is comprehensive and thorough, invariably suited to the exigencies of the moment. If matters are indeed as he says, pacifying the Japanese raiders would be no great task. Those who understand the affairs of their time are outstanding men—who could this be but you?”

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
以覈實為效又識今弊之最要者使子策盡行
倭可計日平矣取之不獨以其文也
考試官大學士李批倭患屢歲不平非無策之
患而不着實舉行之罪也子之言其真知要
者乎
執事策士以平倭至計而愚非其人也雖
然請陳其槩焉夫北虜南夷古所同患然
以愚言之虜固可慮未若南之甚也今諸
邊迫近虜稍稍牧馬長城之外窺隙而動
===
每三關聲震則九門設防士大夫之所為
慮者也以其近也然惟其近則虜之一入
羽檄朝馳而夕聞是虜情不能掩也而諸
將懼于震驚罪在反掌罔不疾驅恐有弗
逮是諸將不遑息也而南則遠矣賊猖獗
屠戮每在頃刻之內而聲聞在月餘之外
雖按事之臣不敢不告而驛使馳至則又
轉而他適矣故賊勢未易詳也賊不易詳
則諸將奮而前驅義不旋踵功狀未易即

羽檄朝馳而夕聞是虜情不能掩也而諸
將懼于震驚罪在反掌罔不疾驅恐有弗
逮是諸將不遑息也而南則遠矣賊猖獗
屠戮每在頃刻之內而聲聞在月餘之外
雖按事之臣不敢不告而驛使馳至則又
轉而他適矣故賊勢未易詳也賊不易詳
則諸將奮而前驅義不旋踵功狀未易即
punctuated:
以覈實為效，又識今弊之最要者。使子策盡行，倭可計日平矣。取之不獨以其文也。
考試官大學士李批：倭患屢歲不平，非無策之患，而不着實舉行之罪也。子之言，其真知要者乎！
執事策士以平倭至計，而愚非其人也。雖然，請陳其槩焉。夫北虜南夷，古所同患，然以愚言之，虜固可慮，未若南之甚也。今諸邊迫近虜，稍稍牧馬長城之外，窺隙而動。每三關聲震，則九門設防，士大夫之所為慮者也，以其近也。然惟其近，則虜之一入，羽檄朝馳而夕聞，是虜情不能掩也。而諸將懼于震驚，罪在反掌，罔不疾驅，恐有弗逮，是諸將不遑息也。而南則遠矣。賊猖獗屠戮，每在頃刻之內，而聲聞在月餘之外。雖按事之臣不敢不告，而驛使馳至，則又轉而他適矣。故賊勢未易詳也。賊不易詳，則諸將奮而前驅，義不旋踵，功狀未易即
translation_en:
…Taking the verification of actual circumstances as the measure of effectiveness, you also recognize the most crucial of today’s abuses. If all your proposals were implemented, the Japanese raiders could be pacified within a countable number of days. We select this answer for more than its literary merits.
Examiner and Grand Secretary Li comments: The trouble with the Japanese raiders has remained unsettled year after year. The problem is not a lack of plans; the fault lies in failing to put them into actual practice. Your words surely show a true understanding of what matters!
You, honored examiners, have tested the candidates with a policy question on the best plan for pacifying the Japanese raiders, yet I am not the person qualified to answer it. Nevertheless, allow me to set out its broad outlines. The northern barbarians and the southern aliens have both been sources of trouble since antiquity. In my humble view, however, although the northern barbarians certainly give cause for concern, their threat is not as grave as that in the south. Our frontier regions now lie close to the northern barbarians, who gradually pasture their horses outside the Great Wall, watching for openings before making their move. Whenever alarm resounds through the Three Passes, defenses are established at the capital’s Nine Gates. This is what concerns the scholar-officials, because the enemy is so near. Yet precisely because they are near, whenever the northern barbarians invade, urgent military dispatches sent off in the morning are heard of by evening. Thus the enemy’s circumstances cannot be concealed. Moreover, the commanders fear the alarm caused at court, knowing that punishment could come in an instant. All hasten forward, fearing they may fail to arrive in time. Thus the commanders have no leisure to rest.
The south, however, is far away. The raiders’ savage slaughter often takes place in moments, while news arrives only after more than a month. Although the officials investigating events dare not fail to report them, by the time the relay messenger arrives, the raiders have already moved elsewhere. Hence it is difficult to obtain a detailed understanding of their situation. Since their situation is difficult to ascertain, even when commanders press boldly forward, resolved by duty never to turn back, the particulars of their achievements cannot readily be immediately…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
明而苟見勢遠冀少須臾毋死以自偷惰
或得以亂名實故諸將未易盡核也此遠
近之勢然也虜部落散處每將南下則會
諸酋長先時備糗餱約期日待報而後發
誠謹間諜可預知也師行遠不過百里諸
邊皆控關阨當虜所至據險以待之猶可
支也今倭與諸夷雜處海島中皆與瀕海
諸郡相直當春風時舟瞬息千里方傳言
倭至或然或否而顧視倭已在左右矣其
===
情難知也中國所恃險者海而已而賊在
諸島中則是險與共之故其來難制也此
難易之勢然也故愚以為可慮者非謂虜
弱而倭強也又非謂虜不足畏也謂其勢
不同也愚請因明問而謹條其事其大者
蓋有七焉其一曰議將其二曰議守令其
三曰議兵其四曰議財其五曰議援其六
曰議守其七曰議防海此七議者固游談
者之常言而當事者之所易厭也然而不

明，而苟見勢遠，冀少須臾毋死，以自偷惰，或得以亂名實，故諸將未易盡核也。此遠近之勢然也。虜部落散處，每將南下，則會諸酋長，先時備糗餱，約期日，待報而後發。誠謹間諜，可預知也。師行遠不過百里，諸邊皆控關阨，當虜所至，據險以待之，猶可支也。今倭與諸夷雜處海島中，皆與瀕海諸郡相直。當春風時，舟瞬息千里，方傳言倭至，或然或否，而顧視倭已在左右矣。其情難知也。中國所恃險者，海而已，而賊在諸島中，則是險與共之，故其來難制也。此難易之勢然也。故愚以為可慮者，非謂虜弱而倭強也，又非謂虜不足畏也，謂其勢不同也。
愚請因明問而謹條其事，其大者蓋有七焉。其一曰議將，其二曰議守令，其三曰議兵，其四曰議財，其五曰議援，其六曰議守，其七曰議防海。此七議者，固游談者之常言，而當事者之所易厭也，然而不
translation_en:
…be made clear at once. But if, seeing that they are far removed, commanders merely hope to survive a few moments longer and indulge their own indolence, they may succeed in confusing reputation with actual performance. Thus it is difficult to assess all the commanders thoroughly. This results from the differing circumstances of distance and proximity. The northern raiders’ tribes live scattered apart. Whenever they intend to move south, they assemble their chieftains, prepare dry provisions in advance, agree upon a date, and wait for word before setting out. If intelligence work is conducted diligently, their movements can be known beforehand. Their forces march no farther than a hundred li; the frontier positions all command strategic passes and defiles. By occupying defensible ground where the raiders are approaching and awaiting them there, we can still hold them off. Now the Japanese raiders dwell among other foreign peoples on the offshore islands, all directly opposite our coastal prefectures. When the spring winds blow, their ships cover a thousand li in an instant. Just as reports begin circulating that the Japanese raiders have arrived, with uncertainty over whether they are true, one looks around to find the raiders already close at hand. Their movements are difficult to ascertain. The natural barrier on which China relies is simply the sea; yet because the bandits inhabit the islands, this barrier is shared with them. Thus their incursions are difficult to check. This accounts for the difference in difficulty between the two situations. Hence, when I say that there is cause for concern, I do not mean that the northern raiders are weak and the Japanese raiders strong, nor that the northern raiders need not be feared. I mean that their circumstances differ.
In response to your enlightened question, I venture respectfully to set out the matters involved. There are seven principal points: first, a discussion of commanders; second, of prefects and magistrates; third, of troops; fourth, of finances; fifth, of reinforcements; sixth, of defense; and seventh, of coastal defense. These seven topics are admittedly the stock talk of idle discoursers, which those responsible for affairs readily grow tired of hearing. Nevertheless, they must not …

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
可易也愚聞古之遣將者或誓于軍中或
誓于軍門之外或將交刃而誓所以一志
而定制也故將者君授之制而無所制于
人者也昔孫武為吳將兵未試而斬隊長
穰苴為齊將始出而斬監軍此二子者非
好殺以明威也子公伐郅支延壽欲請之
而不從條侯禦七國梁王數趣之而不動
此二子者又非執已以忤物也然且行之
則以肅人心而制重也故古者將之于軍
===
如心使臂如臂使指赴湯火投溝壑而無
不從者誠足以制其命也而今也如潰土
如潰癰敗則不可收拾將與俱靡而已此
最今之大患也愚以為將必先有天下之
識具命世之才自知其足以任矣然後不
辭而受之因察彼已審虛實慮時當否具
列其狀請少寬日月一切得以自内如有
不効願伏斧鑕既得請矣然後臥薪席藁
誓不與此賊並立入忘其家出忘其身淬

可易也。愚聞古之遣將者，或誓于軍中，或誓于軍門之外，或將交刃而誓，所以一志而定制也。故將者，君授之制，而無所制于人者也。昔孫武為吳將，兵未試而斬隊長；穰苴為齊將，始出而斬監軍。此二子者，非好殺以明威也。子公伐郅支，延壽欲請之而不從；條侯禦七國，梁王數趣之而不動。此二子者，又非執已以忤物也。然且行之，則以肅人心而制重也。故古者將之于軍，如心使臂，如臂使指，赴湯火，投溝壑，而無不從者，誠足以制其命也。而今也，如潰土，如潰癰，敗則不可收拾，將與俱靡而已。此最今之大患也。
愚以為將必先有天下之識，具命世之才，自知其足以任矣，然後不辭而受之。因察彼已，審虛實，慮時當否，具列其狀，請少寬日月，一切得以自内。如有不効，願伏斧鑕。既得請矣，然後臥薪席藁，誓不與此賊並立，入忘其家，出忘其身，淬
translation_en:
…they cannot be treated lightly. I have heard that, when commanders were dispatched in antiquity, they sometimes administered an oath within the army, sometimes outside the camp gate, and sometimes just before blades crossed. This served to unite the soldiers’ resolve and establish command. A commander thus receives authority from his ruler and is subject to no one else’s control. Formerly, when Sun Wu commanded the army of Wu, he executed the company leaders before the troops had been put to the test; when Rangju commanded the army of Qi, he executed the Army Supervisor just as he set out. These two men did not delight in killing merely to display their might. When Zigong attacked Zhizhi, Yanshou wished to request authorization, but Zigong would not agree; when the Marquis of Tiao resisted the Seven Kingdoms, the Prince of Liang repeatedly pressed him to act, but he remained unmoved. Nor were these two men simply insisting on their own way in defiance of others. Rather, they acted thus to instill discipline in men’s hearts and lend weight to their command. Hence, in antiquity, a commander directed his army as the mind directs the arm and the arm directs the fingers. Whether ordered into boiling water and fire or into ditches and ravines, none failed to obey, for he truly possessed sufficient authority over their lives. Today, however, armies are like crumbling earth or a bursting abscess: once defeated, they cannot be put back in order, and their commanders merely fall with them. This is the greatest of the present dangers.
In my humble view, a commander must first possess an understanding of affairs throughout the realm and talents exceptional in his age. Only when he knows himself capable of the responsibility should he accept it without declining. He should then examine the enemy and his own side, assess their weaknesses and strengths, consider whether the timing is suitable, and set out the circumstances in full. He should request a little more time and permission to handle everything on his own authority [?], pledging that, should he fail to achieve results, he is willing to submit to the executioner’s axe and block. Once his request has been granted, he should sleep on firewood and use straw as his mat, swearing never to coexist with these bandits. At home he should forget his family, and in the field forget his own person, tempering…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
礪奮發天地可感而金石可破也盖三軍
之志竦矣然後左援鼓右援旗申衆而誓
之取其不率者罪之于庭以令三軍又取
其甚者縣頭于門以令衆其令一新矣然
後陳金于廡縣格于外有士從中吐竒撫
劍躍而出焉則賞之不踰時有士從外提
戈斬級躍而入焉則賞之不踰時士皆超
距作矣有將如此則其氣足以橫海上而
目無倭夷矣軍安得不壯功安得不成故
===
有將則其他便宜皆末計也故一曰議將
然將者折衝于上者也而守令者保障于
下者也將之所轄者廣而守令之所守者
專如使守令能用其民則諸郡邑皆兵也
否則將以賊所至而用兵兵不得不寡如
使守令能率其民以禦賊則賊所至皆敵
也否則將禦其東而賊轉而西將禦其南
而賊轉而北賊無端而將所禦之力有限
將不得不勞兵寡而將勞立敝之道也故

礪奮發，天地可感，而金石可破也。盖三軍之志竦矣，然後左援鼓，右援旗，申衆而誓之，取其不率者罪之于庭，以令三軍；又取其甚者縣頭于門，以令衆。其令一新矣，然後陳金于廡，縣格于外。有士從中吐竒，撫劍躍而出焉，則賞之不踰時；有士從外提戈斬級，躍而入焉，則賞之不踰時。士皆超距作矣。有將如此，則其氣足以橫海上，而目無倭夷矣。軍安得不壯？功安得不成？故有將，則其他便宜皆末計也。故一曰議將。
然將者折衝于上者也，而守令者保障于下者也。將之所轄者廣，而守令之所守者專。如使守令能用其民，則諸郡邑皆兵也；否則將以賊所至而用兵，兵不得不寡。如使守令能率其民以禦賊，則賊所至皆敵也；否則將禦其東，而賊轉而西；將禦其南，而賊轉而北。賊無端，而將所禦之力有限，將不得不勞。兵寡而將勞，立敝之道也。故
translation_en:
…temper themselves and rouse their resolve: they can move Heaven and Earth and shatter metal and stone. Once the resolve of the entire army has been stirred, the commander should take up the drum on his left and the banner on his right, reiterate his commands to the assembled men, and bind them by an oath. He should punish those who disobey in the courtyard as a warning to the entire army; for the gravest offenders, he should hang their heads at the gate as a warning to the men. Once military discipline has thus been renewed, he should display gold in the covered corridors and post the schedule of rewards outside. If a soldier emerges from the ranks with an ingenious plan, grasping his sword and springing forward, reward him without delay. If a soldier returns from outside carrying his weapon and the heads he has taken, bounding into camp, reward him without delay. The soldiers will all leap into action. With such a commander, their spirit will suffice to sweep across the seas, and they will regard the Japanese barbarians as nothing. How could the army fail to be strong? How could success fail to follow? Thus, once there is a capable commander, all other expedient measures are secondary considerations. Hence my first proposal is to consider the choice of commanders.
Yet commanders repel aggression at the higher level, while prefects and magistrates provide protection at the local level. A commander’s jurisdiction is extensive, whereas the charge of a prefect or magistrate is concentrated. If prefects and magistrates can mobilize their people, every prefecture and county will have troops. Otherwise, the commander must deploy troops wherever the raiders arrive, and his forces will inevitably be too few. If prefects and magistrates can lead their people in resisting the raiders, the raiders will encounter opponents wherever they go. Otherwise, when the commander defends the east, the raiders will turn west; when he defends the south, they will turn north. The raiders’ movements have no fixed pattern, while the commander’s defensive strength is limited: he will inevitably become exhausted. Too few troops and an exhausted commander are a sure path to immediate collapse. Thus…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
李廣守北平而匈奴避邊魏尚為雲中守
而虜不敢犯龔遂為渤海而盜賊散魯恭
至樂安而渠帥降此其已然之效也其法
莫如使部使者察東南諸郡守令之宜而
易置之又使天下部使者皆察其可為東
南者上之銓司又使諸臺諫徧察中外以
請又使銓司按諸察舉擇其宜而授之如
賊小至則各以其地戰大至則固守其地
以待能固守者與戰勝者同賞賞必速玩
===
===
寇者與將同罰罰必重如此則守令與將
同心而諸郡邑與幕府同體合而為一以
禦賊尚何賊之不滅哉故二曰議守令愚
聞之將不知兵以其地與敵也兵不知教
以其將與敵也今議者不惟兵之不練而
數欲調兵昔山東兵常調矣而無捄于敗
狼廣兵再調矣而無捄于敗蕃土兵又調
矣無捄于敗而害益滋其所至如乳虎而
其臨陣如鳥散居則為民蠹出則長賊威

===

以其將與敵也今議者不惟兵之不練而
數欲調兵昔山東兵常調矣而無捄于敗
淮廣兵再調矣而無捄于敗蓄土兵又調
矣無捄于敗而害益滋其所至如乳虎而
其臨陣如鳥散居則為民蠹出則長賊威
punctuated:
李廣守北平，而匈奴避邊；魏尚為雲中守，而虜不敢犯；龔遂為渤海，而盜賊散；魯恭至樂安，而渠帥降。此其已然之效也。其法莫如使部使者察東南諸郡守令之宜而易置之，又使天下部使者皆察其可為東南者，上之銓司；又使諸臺諫徧察中外以請；又使銓司按諸察舉，擇其宜而授之。如賊小至，則各以其地戰；大至，則固守其地以待。能固守者與戰勝者同賞，賞必速；玩寇者與將同罰，罰必重。如此，則守令與將同心，而諸郡邑與幕府同體，合而為一以禦賊，尚何賊之不滅哉？故二曰議守令。

愚聞之：將不知兵，以其地與敵也；兵不知教，以其將與敵也。今議者不惟兵之不練，而數欲調兵。昔山東兵常調矣，而無捄于敗；狼廣兵再調矣，而無捄于敗；蕃土兵又調矣，無捄于敗，而害益滋。其所至如乳虎，而其臨陣如鳥散；居則為民蠹，出則長賊威。
translation_en:
…Li Guang defended Beiping, and the Xiongnu kept away from the frontier; Wei Shang served as governor of Yunzhong, and the enemy dared not invade; Gong Sui governed Bohai, and the bandits dispersed; Lu Gong arrived in Le’an, and the bandit chieftains surrendered. These are proven results. The best method would be to have the regional inspecting commissioners examine the suitability of the prefects and county magistrates throughout the southeast and replace or reassign them accordingly. The inspecting commissioners throughout the empire should also identify men capable of serving in the southeast and submit their names to the personnel selection authorities. The censors and supervising secretaries should likewise examine officials throughout the capital and the provinces and submit recommendations. The personnel selection authorities should then review these assessments and nominations, select suitable men, and appoint them. If the bandits come in small numbers, each official should fight within his own jurisdiction; if they come in force, he should hold his territory securely and await assistance. Those who hold their ground should receive the same rewards as those victorious in battle, and rewards must be swift. Those who treat the bandits lightly should receive the same punishments as generals, and punishments must be severe. In this way, prefects and county magistrates would share a common purpose with the generals, and the prefectures and counties would form one body with the military headquarters, joining together to resist the bandits. What bandits could then escape destruction? Thus, my second proposal concerns prefects and county magistrates.

I have heard that when a general does not understand warfare, he hands his territory to the enemy; when soldiers have not been trained, they hand their general to the enemy. Yet those discussing the matter today disregard the troops’ lack of training and repeatedly seek to transfer more troops. Previously, troops from Shandong were regularly transferred, yet they could not avert defeat. Lang and Guang troops [?] were transferred again, yet they could not avert defeat. Tribal and native troops were then transferred, but they too could not avert defeat, while the harm only increased. Wherever they arrive, they are like tigresses with cubs; when they face battle, they scatter like birds. In garrison they prey upon the people; in the field they enhance the bandits’ might…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
□民苦調兵與被賊等以其遣之不精而
馭之無統也夫兵法平原曠野此用衆之
地也如羣鹿抗獐以多者勝道狹險要則
如兩鼠闘穴以勇者勝雖衆無所用也故
我軍千人並進而賊以數人舞刀橫行稍
剉其前則後皆反走千人皆廢矣故兵而
有制則淮陰驅市人而勝泜上即無制也
苻堅以四十萬而敗于淝兵多則難制難
制則易敗此其明驗也故莫若練土著之
===
兵然始練不可以應卒而調兵不可以持
久莫若稍減其調而徐俟其練調簡則易
精練久則愈習精則土著之兵益奮習則
調兵可以益減此互相輔而終相省也其
法則分責守令而總責之將非愚所能悉
數也故三曰議兵愚嘗思今坐困之術莫
有過于兵多者方其兵之初調縣縣傳送
其道里之費不可勝言也所過鹵掠其騷
動之費不可勝言也至則家給而户養之

馭之無紀也夫兵法平原曠野此用衆之

如兩鼠鬭穴以勇者勝雖衆無所用也故
我軍千人並進而賊以數人揮刀横行稍
到其前則後皆反走千人皆廢矣故兵而
有制則淮陰驅市人而勝泜上即無制也
符堅以四十萬而敗于淝兵多則難制難
制則易敗此其明驗也故莫若練土著之
===

調兵可以益減此互相輔而終相省也其

數也故三曰議兵愚嘗思今坐困之術莫

其道里之費不可勝言也所過鹵掠其騷
動之費不可勝言也至則家給而戶養之
punctuated:
□民苦調兵與被賊等，以其遣之不精而馭之無統也。夫兵法，平原曠野，此用衆之地也，如羣鹿抗獐，以多者勝；道狹險要，則如兩鼠闘穴，以勇者勝，雖衆無所用也。故我軍千人並進，而賊以數人舞刀橫行，稍剉其前，則後皆反走，千人皆廢矣。故兵而有制，則淮陰驅市人而勝泜上；即無制也，苻堅以四十萬而敗于淝。兵多則難制，難制則易敗，此其明驗也。故莫若練土著之兵。然始練不可以應卒，而調兵不可以持久，莫若稍減其調而徐俟其練。調簡則易精，練久則愈習；精則土著之兵益奮，習則調兵可以益減。此互相輔而終相省也。其法則分責守令，而總責之將，非愚所能悉數也。故三曰議兵。
愚嘗思今坐困之術，莫有過于兵多者。方其兵之初調，縣縣傳送，其道里之費不可勝言也；所過鹵掠，其騷動之費不可勝言也；至則家給而户養之。
translation_en:
…[Illegible] the people suffer as much from troop deployments as from attacks by the bandits, because the troops dispatched are not carefully selected and their command is not unified. In warfare, open plains and broad fields are places where numbers can be employed: like a herd of deer contending with water deer, the more numerous side wins. On narrow roads and at strategic defiles, however, it is like two rats fighting in a hole: the braver wins, and even great numbers are of no use. Thus a thousand of our soldiers advance together, yet only a few bandits brandishing swords move boldly across their path. Once they slightly check the men in front, all those behind turn and flee, rendering the entire thousand useless. With properly organized troops, the Lord of Huaiyin could lead men from the marketplace to victory on the Zhi River; without such organization, Fu Jian was defeated at the Fei River with four hundred thousand men. Numerous troops are hard to control, and troops that are hard to control are easily defeated: these are clear proofs. Nothing, therefore, is better than training local troops. Yet troops just beginning their training cannot meet sudden emergencies, while bringing in troops from elsewhere cannot be sustained indefinitely. It would be best gradually to reduce such deployments while patiently allowing local training to take effect. With fewer troops brought in, it is easier to ensure their quality; with prolonged training, local troops become increasingly practiced. The excellence of the former will further encourage the local troops, and as the latter become practiced, outside deployments can be reduced still further. The two measures thus reinforce each other and ultimately yield savings. As for the methods, responsibility should be apportioned among prefects and county magistrates, with overall responsibility assigned to the commander; I cannot enumerate all the details. Hence my third proposal is to deliberate on the troops.
I have often reflected that, among the practices now bringing us into distress, none is worse than maintaining too many troops. When troops are first mobilized, each county forwards them to the next, and the expenses of their journey are beyond reckoning. They plunder wherever they pass, and the costs of the resulting disruption are beyond reckoning. Once they arrive, every family must supply them and every household maintain them…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
供餉益繁而鹵掠不息其費又不可勝言
也此自竭其源者也今議者不惟兵多之
費而憂財之乏此所謂舛也因其乏而議
加賦益財此又舛之舛者也昔先零之役
當其兵集耿中丞糴四十萬穀而不足及
充國罷騎兵般師不費斗穀而羌平人皆
知充國屯田之興利而不知般師之省費
也故調兵一而當練兵之費百養調兵一
而當土著之兵其費十調益簡則費益省
===
以其所費者而練士何弗強也以其所省
者而充費何弗贍也此不加益而足財之
道也故四曰議財夫列地定制犬牙相入
所以相衛也封疆相錯所以相保也緩則
相安急則相救非苟自全而已也故春秋
隣國不能救則譏之桓公不能恤小則譏
之此天下之大誼也漢右渠之伐兩將軍
異同而朝鮮幾危唐祿山之變而賀蘭擁
兵睢陽遂陷此天下之大機也今地壤相

punctuated:
供餉益繁，而鹵掠不息，其費又不可勝言也。此自竭其源者也。今議者不惟兵多之費，而憂財之乏，此所謂舛也。因其乏而議加賦益財，此又舛之舛者也。昔先零之役，當其兵集，耿中丞糴四十萬穀而不足；及充國罷騎兵般師，不費斗穀而羌平。人皆知充國屯田之興利，而不知般師之省費也。故調兵一，而當練兵之費百；養調兵一，而當土著之兵其費十。調益簡，則費益省。以其所費者而練士，何弗強也？以其所省者而充費，何弗贍也？此不加益而足財之道也。故四曰議財。
夫列地定制，犬牙相入，所以相衛也；封疆相錯，所以相保也。緩則相安，急則相救，非苟自全而已也。故《春秋》隣國不能救則譏之，桓公不能恤小則譏之。此天下之大誼也。漢右渠之伐，兩將軍異同而朝鮮幾危；唐祿山之變，而賀蘭擁兵，睢陽遂陷。此天下之大機也。今地壤相
translation_en:
…the provision of supplies becomes increasingly burdensome, while plundering continues unabated; the expense of this, too, is beyond reckoning. This is to exhaust one's own resources. Those now debating the matter overlook the expense of maintaining so many troops and worry instead about the shortage of funds. This is what is meant by getting things wrong. To respond to that shortage by proposing higher taxes to increase revenue compounds the error.
During the campaign against the Xianling, when the troops assembled, Assistant Geng (Geng Zhongcheng) purchased four hundred thousand measures of grain, yet even this was insufficient. But when Zhao Chongguo disbanded the cavalry and sent the troops home, the Qiang were pacified without the expenditure of a single peck of grain. Everyone knows the benefits produced by Chongguo's military agricultural colonies, but they do not recognize the savings achieved by sending the troops home. Thus, mobilizing one soldier costs as much as training a hundred; maintaining one mobilized soldier costs as much as maintaining ten local soldiers. The fewer troops mobilized, the greater the savings. If the money expended on mobilization were used to train soldiers, how could they fail to become strong? If the savings were used to meet expenses, how could funds fail to suffice? This is the way to secure adequate funds without increasing taxation. Hence my fourth proposal is to deliberate on finances.
Now, in dividing territory and establishing its organization, boundaries interlock like a dog's teeth so that the regions may defend one another; their frontiers overlap so that they may protect one another. In peaceful times they keep one another secure; in emergencies they come to one another's aid. Their purpose is more than merely to preserve themselves. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals censures neighboring states when they fail to provide relief, and censures Duke Huan when he fails to care for smaller states. This is a great principle of righteousness for all under Heaven. During the Han campaign against Youqu, disagreement between the two generals nearly brought disaster in Chaoxian [?]. During the Tang rebellion of Lushan, Helan held his troops back, and Suiyang consequently fell. This is a matter on which the fate of the realm turns. Today, the territories adjoin one another…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
接而坐視勝敗令賊長驅深入而無顧忌
之心此甚不可長也愚以為宜特嚴其法
約曰賊攻西則東出銳師擊其左賊東則
亦如之賊攻南則北出銳師繞其後賊北
則亦如之賊攻中則左右前後各出銳師
四面而起非其守地而兵先至者有異賞
坐視其隣之敗者與同罰則是賊腹背受
敵而我多樹兵也賊亦安能肆而不顧哉
此最多方弭賊之道而今日之要務也故
===
五曰議援夫待援莫先于守未有榦弱而
枝扶者也然守必以戰而守城必以野自
法有陷城之誅而未嚴殘野之罰賊至則
苟負孤城而棄其四境煙焰相望號聲相
聞所至蕭條郭為丘墟誠有所不忍言者
又安望其援乎故李牧備邊先在收保而
不失不能收保是資賊也後將軍燉煌先
在乘隧列障校聯不絕賊不敢犯使疎而
可犯是自敗也愚以為宜畧倣墩堡之制

法有陷城之誅而未嚴殘野之罰賊至則
苟負孤城而棄其四境煙熖相望號聲相
聞所至蕭條郭為丘墟誠有所不忍言者
又安望其援乎故李牧備邊先在收保而
不失不能收保是資賊也後將軍墩煌先
在乘隧列障校聯不絕賊不敢犯使賊而
可犯是自救也愚以為宜畧倣墩堡之制
punctuated:
接而坐視勝敗，令賊長驅深入而無顧忌之心，此甚不可長也。愚以為宜特嚴其法，約曰：賊攻西，則東出銳師擊其左；賊東，則亦如之。賊攻南，則北出銳師繞其後；賊北，則亦如之。賊攻中，則左右前後各出銳師，四面而起。非其守地而兵先至者，有異賞；坐視其隣之敗者，與同罰。則是賊腹背受敵，而我多樹兵也。賊亦安能肆而不顧哉？此最多方弭賊之道，而今日之要務也。故五曰議援。
夫待援莫先于守，未有榦弱而枝扶者也。然守必以戰，而守城必以野。自法有陷城之誅，而未嚴殘野之罰，賊至則苟負孤城而棄其四境。煙焰相望，號聲相聞，所至蕭條，郭為丘墟，誠有所不忍言者。又安望其援乎？故李牧備邊，先在收保而不失；不能收保，是資賊也。後將軍燉煌，先在乘隧列障，校聯不絕，賊不敢犯；使疎而可犯，是自敗也。愚以為宜畧倣墩堡之制。
translation_en:
…adjoin one another, yet they stand by and watch victory or defeat, allowing the bandits to drive far into the interior without apprehension. This must certainly not be allowed to continue. In my humble opinion, the regulations should be made especially strict, stipulating: when the bandits attack the west, the east must dispatch picked troops to strike their left flank; when they attack the east, the same principle applies. When the bandits attack the south, the north must dispatch picked troops to circle behind them; when they attack the north, the same principle applies. When the bandits attack the center, picked troops must be dispatched from left and right, front and rear, rising against them on all four sides. Those whose troops arrive first, even though the threatened territory is outside their assigned defense area, should receive exceptional rewards. Those who stand by and watch their neighbors suffer defeat should share their punishment. Thus the bandits will face enemies both front and rear, while we deploy troops at many points. How could the bandits then act recklessly without looking to their own safety? This is the most versatile means of suppressing bandits and an urgent task today. Hence my fifth proposal is to deliberate on reinforcements.
Now, in awaiting reinforcements, nothing takes precedence over defense: never has a weak trunk been held up by its branches. Yet defense necessarily depends on fighting, and defending a city necessarily depends on defending the countryside. Since the law provides capital punishment for the loss of a city but has not imposed strict penalties for the devastation of the countryside, when bandits arrive, defenders merely rely on an isolated city and abandon all its surrounding territory. Smoke and flames are visible from place to place; cries can be heard from one place to another. Wherever the bandits go, desolation follows, and the outer settlements become heaps of ruins. There are truly things one cannot bear to describe. How, then, can one hope for reinforcements? Thus, when Li Mu defended the frontier, his first concern was to gather the people into protection and keep them safe. Failure to gather and protect them supplies the bandits with resources. The General of the Rear at Dunhuang [?] gave priority to manning beacon towers and arranging fortified posts, with the military units linked in an unbroken chain [?], so that the bandits dared not attack. To leave gaps that permit attack is to bring defeat upon oneself. In my humble opinion, we should broadly follow the system of watchtowers and forts…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
使民各聚為市市列為堡約其道里之中
使勢可相及每賊至則墩堡固守而郡縣
急趨而助之而又特嚴其法使四境殘甚
者與失城同罪則人各為戰地各為守賊
入而無所得其勢自困矣故六曰議守雖
然此皆賊已入之說也夫賊已入則守之
于内而其未入則禦之于海然諸將海戰
而勝者常十七其内地戰者敗常十八非
將勇于海而怯于内也其故有四士卒入
===
海人無還心皆殊死戰無所逃難一也洪
艟巨艦易以陵賊勢便二也毒藥火器且
戰且焚三也賊載水而飲開口待鹵勢不
能持四也而其後不能禦賊者亦有四犯
不測之險以命博賊而賞常不讎生其怠
心一也海中無人易以為解二也既不能
賞易于姑息將不能驅三也海波不常或
利或否四也議者皆言益修戰具反其四
失守馬蹟諸山以控吳守大衢諸山以衛

而勝者常十七其內地戰者敗常十八非
將勇于海而怯于內也其故有四士卒入
===
海人無還心皆殊死戰無所逃難一也洪

戰且焚三也賊載水而飲開口待鹵勢不
能持四也而其後不能禦賊者亦有四犯
不測之險以命博賊而賞常不讐生其忌
心一也海中無人易以為解二也既不能
賞易于姑息將不能驅三也海波不常或
利或否四也議者皆言益修戰具反其四
失守馬蹟諸山以控吳守大衢諸山以衛
punctuated:
使民各聚為市，市列為堡，約其道里之中，使勢可相及。每賊至，則墩堡固守，而郡縣急趨而助之。而又特嚴其法，使四境殘甚者與失城同罪，則人各為戰，地各為守，賊入而無所得，其勢自困矣。故六曰議守。
雖然，此皆賊已入之說也。夫賊已入，則守之于内；而其未入，則禦之于海。然諸將海戰而勝者常十七，其内地戰者敗常十八，非將勇于海而怯于内也。其故有四：士卒入海，人無還心，皆殊死戰，無所逃難，一也；洪艟巨艦，易以陵賊，勢便，二也；毒藥火器，且戰且焚，三也；賊載水而飲，開口待鹵，勢不能持，四也。而其後不能禦賊者亦有四：犯不測之險，以命博賊，而賞常不讎，生其怠心，一也；海中無人，易以為解，二也；既不能賞，易于姑息，將不能驅，三也；海波不常，或利或否，四也。議者皆言益修戰具，反其四失，守馬蹟諸山以控吳，守大衢諸山以衛
translation_en:
…have the people gather into market settlements, and organize these settlements into forts, placing them at suitable intervals so that they can support one another. Whenever raiders arrive, the watchtowers and forts should hold firm, while the prefectural and county authorities hasten to their aid. Moreover, make the law especially strict: those who allow severe devastation throughout their jurisdictions should incur the same punishment as those who lose a city. Then everyone will fight, and every place will be defended. When the raiders enter and gain nothing, their strength will naturally be exhausted. Thus the sixth point is to deliberate on defense.
Nevertheless, all this concerns raiders who have already entered our territory. Once they have entered, we must defend against them inland; before they enter, we must repel them at sea. Yet our commanders win seven out of ten engagements at sea, whereas they lose eight out of ten engagements inland. This is not because they are brave at sea and cowardly inland. There are four reasons. First, when the soldiers go to sea, none thinks of turning back: all fight to the death, having nowhere to escape danger. Second, large warships and immense vessels make it easy to overpower the raiders, giving us an advantageous position. Third, poisonous substances and firearms allow us to fight and burn them at the same time. Fourth, the raiders must carry their drinking water aboard; with mouths open, they await brine [?], and cannot sustain their position.
There are also four reasons why subsequently we have been unable to repel the raiders. First, our men brave unpredictable dangers and stake their lives against the raiders, yet their rewards are often not commensurate, which makes them slacken their efforts. Second, there is no one at sea to witness events, making excuses easy. Third, since adequate rewards cannot be given, indulgence readily follows, and commanders cannot drive their men forward. Fourth, conditions at sea are inconstant, sometimes favorable and sometimes not. Those discussing the matter all urge us to improve our fighting equipment further, remedy these four shortcomings, hold Maji and the neighboring islands to secure Wu, and hold Daqu and the neighboring islands to defend…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
越守陳錢諸島以制賊往来之衝夾擊互
救三道鼎峙賊不足防矣故七日議防海
然愚又聞善計者當反其始詳慮者當要
其終自
明興以来防倭之法備矣當是時信國江夏築
城起自登萊至浙沿海凡五十九城費非
不甚大也籍民丁四之一以戍人非不甚
勞也設衛置所間以烽堠其故基纍然猶
有存者役非不甚廣也然且為之亦見倭
===
===
之不可不防而
聖祖之遠謨創始慮終甚深遠也此則他日事
定之後亦不可以不徐議者也抑愚又聞
之多言盈庭古之所戒言敢塞耳春秋患
焉夫計易摇而事失者以其言之者多而
行之者艱也愚所陳列大畧具已酌其可
否而核實其効是在當事者非愚所敢與
聞也雖然愚竊伏草野覩我
皇上聖神文武臨照天下如日月之明也軍國

越守陳錢諸島以制賊往来之衝夾擊互
救三道遇時賊不足防矣故七曰議防海
然愚又聞善計者當反其始詳慮者當要
其終自
明興以来防倭之法備矣當是時信國江夏築
城起自登萊至浙沿海凡五十九城費非
不甚大也籍民丁四之一以戍人非不甚
勞也設衛置所間以烽堠其故基礨然猶
有存者役非不甚廣也然且為之亦見倭
===
聖祖之遠謨創始慮終甚深遠也此則他日事
定之後亦不可以不徐議者也抑愚又聞
之不可不防而
之多言盈庭古之所戒言取塞耳春秋患
馬矢計易搖而事失者以其言之者多而
行之者鮮也愚所陳列大畧具已酌其可
否而核實其効是在當事者非愚所敢與
聞也雖然愚竊伏草野覩我
皇上聖神文武臨照天下如日月之明也軍國
punctuated:
越，守陳錢諸島以制賊往来之衝，夾擊互救，三道鼎峙，賊不足防矣。故七日議防海。然愚又聞，善計者當反其始，詳慮者當要其終。自明興以来，防倭之法備矣。當是時，信國、江夏築城，起自登萊至浙，沿海凡五十九城，費非不甚大也；籍民丁四之一以戍，人非不甚勞也；設衛置所，間以烽堠，其故基纍然猶有存者，役非不甚廣也。然且為之，亦見倭之不可不防，而聖祖之遠謨，創始慮終，甚深遠也。此則他日事定之後，亦不可以不徐議者也。
抑愚又聞之，多言盈庭，古之所戒；言敢塞耳，春秋患焉。夫計易摇而事失者，以其言之者多，而行之者艱也。愚所陳列，大畧具已；酌其可否而核實其効，是在當事者，非愚所敢與聞也。雖然，愚竊伏草野，覩我皇上聖神文武，臨照天下，如日月之明也。軍國
translation_en:
…Yue; hold Chenqian and the other islands to control the strategic passages by which the raiders come and go. Strike them from both sides and provide mutual support: with these three defensive sectors standing like the legs of a tripod, the raiders would be no great difficulty to ward off. Thus the seventh point [?] concerns coastal defense. Yet I have also heard that those who plan well should return to the beginnings, and those who deliberate thoroughly should take account of the outcome. Since the founding of the Ming, measures for defense against the Japanese raiders have been comprehensive. At that time, the Duke of Xin and the Duke of Jiangxia built fifty-nine walled fortifications along the coast, from Dengzhou and Laizhou to Zhejiang. The expense was indeed very great. One in every four adult male commoners was registered for garrison service: the people's toil was indeed very heavy. Guards and battalions were established, with beacon towers interspersed among them; their old foundations still survive in many places. The labor required was indeed extensive. Yet these measures were undertaken nonetheless, showing both that defense against the Japanese raiders was indispensable and that the sagely founding emperor's far-reaching plans, considering the outcome from the outset, were profoundly farsighted. These, too, are matters that must be deliberated upon in due course once the present troubles have been settled.
I have also heard that a court filled with excessive talk was something the ancients warned against; words that dare to stop up the ears [?] were regarded as a danger in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Plans are readily unsettled and undertakings fail because those who speak are numerous, while putting their words into practice is difficult. The broad outline of what I have set forth is now complete. Weighing its feasibility and verifying its actual effectiveness rest with those responsible for affairs; these are not matters in which I presume to have a say. Nevertheless, dwelling humbly in the countryside, I behold our emperor, sagely and divinely wise, accomplished in civil and military affairs, illuminating all under Heaven as brightly as the sun and moon. Military and state…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
大事先機立斷
威行不測如雷霆之震也薄海内外輻輳歸
命莫有踰于此時者當同符堯舜而邁商
周遠矣書稱蠻夷有苗所以益彰帝德詩
載淮夷獫狁所以益見中興漢人所謂備
驅除而開大聖者也蕞爾之夷行且蕩滅
又何慮焉

punctuated: 大事，先機立斷；威行不測，如雷霆之震也。薄海内外，輻輳歸命，莫有踰于此時者。當同符堯舜，而邁商周遠矣。《書》稱蠻夷有苗，所以益彰帝德；《詩》載淮夷獫狁，所以益見中興。漢人所謂備驅除而開大聖者也。蕞爾之夷，行且蕩滅，又何慮焉？
translation_en: …in great affairs, he anticipates the critical moment and decides at once; his might operates beyond reckoning, like the shock of thunder. Throughout the realm and beyond, all converge like spokes at a hub to submit to his authority; never has this surpassed the present age. He surely matches Yao and Shun and far surpasses the Shang and Zhou. The Book of Documents mentions the Man and Yi peoples and the Youmiao, thereby further displaying the emperor’s virtue; the Book of Odes records the Huaiyi and Xianyun, thereby further revealing the dynastic resurgence. This is what men of the Han called serving to clear the way and prepare the advent of a great sage. These paltry barbarians will soon be utterly swept away. What further cause is there for concern?

會試錄後序

嘉靖丙辰春，禮部當會試天下士。上俞尚書臣用賔等請，特詔大學士臣本輟直侍，往柄其事，臣臺亦濫從焉。既祗命竣役，乃登内外諸執事暨中式士之氏名，并所試文之優者，如故事成錄以獻。臣臺宜有言序後。臣惟天生人而作之君，欲其履尊圖大，萬事咸承乎理也，則必翼輔之以天下之賢材。人君思賢
translation_en:
Postface to the Metropolitan Examination Record

In the spring of the bingchen year of Jiajing [1556], the Ministry of Rites was to conduct the Metropolitan Examination for scholars from throughout the realm. His Majesty approved the request of your servant Yongbin, Minister of Rites, and his colleagues, and specially commanded your servant Ben, Grand Secretary, to suspend his attendance at court and take charge of the examination. Your servant Tai also had the undeserved privilege of joining him.

Having respectfully fulfilled the command and completed our duties, we entered the names of all officials serving within and outside the examination compound, together with those of the successful candidates, and included the best examination compositions. Following precedent, we compiled these into a record for presentation to the throne. It falls to your servant Tai to append some words as a postface.

Your servant reflects that Heaven, in bringing forth the people and establishing a ruler for them, intends him to occupy his exalted position and undertake great designs, so that all affairs accord with principle. It must therefore give him the worthy talents of the realm to assist and support him. A ruler’s concern for worthy…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
材為治理最急不可以易得
也是故養之於未用之先其
教必專而豫擇之於方用之
始其法必慎而精唐虞三代
之盛君恭已而化成士明揚
而績顯盖其效有以致之矣
漢接秦敝迄于有宋上下千
===
數百年間英誼之君代作豈
無矻矻乎政理之勤者而未
聞一庶幾古帝王之治盖賢
材不得其用則繇養與擇之
道失也
明興我
聖祖高皇帝代

材爲治理最急不可以易得
也是故養之於未用之先其
敎必專而豫擇之於方用之
始其法必愼而精唐虞三代
之盛君恭己而化成士明揚
而績顯盖其效有以致之矣
漢接秦敝迄于有宋上下千
===
數百年間英誼之君代作豈
無矻矻乎政理之勤者而未
聞一庶幾古帝王之治盖賢
材不得其用則繇養與擇之
道失也
明興我
聖祖高皇帝代
punctuated:
材為治理最急，不可以易得也。是故養之於未用之先，其教必專而豫；擇之於方用之始，其法必慎而精。唐虞三代之盛，君恭已而化成，士明揚而績顯，盖其效有以致之矣。漢接秦敝，迄于有宋，上下千數百年間，英誼之君代作，豈無矻矻乎政理之勤者？而未聞一庶幾古帝王之治，盖賢材不得其用，則繇養與擇之道失也。
明興，我聖祖高皇帝代
translation_en:
…talent is the most urgent requirement for good government, yet cannot be obtained easily. Therefore, men must be nurtured before they are employed, with instruction that is focused and begun in advance; when they are first to be employed, they must be selected by methods that are careful and exacting. In the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, rulers held themselves reverently and moral transformation was accomplished; worthy men were recognized and promoted, and their achievements became manifest. There were indeed means by which these results were attained. From the Han, which inherited the ruin left by the Qin, down to the Song, over a thousand and several hundred years, heroic and righteous [?] rulers arose in successive ages. Were there none who labored diligently at government? Yet we have not heard of a single one who approached the good government of the ancient emperors and kings. Worthy talent failed to find proper employment because the methods of nurturing and selecting it had gone astray.
When the Ming arose, our Sacred Progenitor, Emperor Gao, acting on behalf of…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
天撫世驅狄氛而廓清之首念賢
材至重故兵革未戢即
究意庠校之事自都邑接乎海
隅荒徼四方萬里之外莫不
立學盖嘗
面諭廷臣謂人材必養之既成
而後用之譬耕稼以求穫也
===
於是建設師徒昭明
訓法以牖迪方內人士其養之
專而豫也如是
御極之再年遂定三歲科舉之制
本經術以黜詞賦嚴考校以

究意庠校之事自都邑接乎海
隅荒徼四方萬里之外莫不

translation_en:
…on Heaven’s behalf, he brought peace to the world, driving out and clearing away the baleful presence of the northern barbarians. His foremost concern was the supreme importance of worthy talent. Thus, even before warfare had ceased, he devoted his attention [?] to schools. From the capitals and cities to the seacoasts and remote frontiers, throughout the realm and beyond ten thousand li, schools were established everywhere. He once personally instructed his court officials that talented men must first be nurtured to maturity and only then employed, just as one tills and plants in order to obtain a harvest.
Accordingly, he established arrangements for teachers and pupils and clarified the rules of instruction, to enlighten and guide the scholars within the realm. Such were his single-minded care and foresight in nurturing them.
In the second year after ascending the throne, he established the system of civil-service examinations held every three years. He made classical learning their foundation, excluding ornate prose and rhapsodies, and made assessment rigorous to eliminate advancement through luck or personal connections. He examined the methods of selecting officials used by successive dynasties and fashioned a balanced system from them. The care and discrimination with which he selected men were likewise…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄

世盖彬彬其選矣肆我
皇上道超邃古統紹先聖

translation_en:
…likewise. Successive sage emperors followed these established regulations, which to this day admit of no alteration. Over the past 190 years, eminent ministers and distinguished counselors have supported splendid government and enhanced the dynasty’s illustrious name. Their achievements shone brightly in their own times: truly, those selected were richly endowed with refinement and substance.
Now our Emperor’s Way surpasses that of remotest antiquity, and his succession continues the tradition of the former sages. He has expounded teachings on reverent single-mindedness, putting them into practice through lectures and study in the official schools. Scholars, whether worthy or foolish, all know to recite and embrace them and are stirred to exert themselves. His gracious virtue has spread everywhere for three twelve-year cycles now. The numerous scholars in their scholarly robes and pendants rejoice in this nurturing and look forward to attaining full accomplishment; its results have already become evident day by day. Could the cultivation of scholars be achieved in a single morning or evening? He has repeatedly commanded the responsible officials to reaffirm the regulations governing the civil-service examinations, prohibiting interpretations of the Classics that depart from the teachings of earlier Confucian scholars and exercising care and gravity in selecting men, indeed…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
視舊加倍矣夫養士以專豫
之教則業守其常而志一擇
士以精慎之法則官得其理
而事勸此我
聖祖所以遺久安長治之道於無
窮者我
皇上籲俊知宅夙夜勤毖故士斐
===
然宣灼於實用旁溢詞藝不
可以曩昔觀也臣頃隸史署
嘗再預校士之末已復司南
考今四入試闈叨典事讀士
之文而推其志察士之志而
占其所從嚮仰窺我
皇上神化斂布徵積於持久士歲
alt_text:
視舊加倍矣夫養士以專隊
之教則業守其常而志一擇
士以精慎之法則官得其理
而事勸此我
聖祖所以遺久安長治之道於無
窮者我
皇上纘俊知宅夙夜勤毖故士斐
===

之文而推其志察士之志而
占其所從竊仰窺我
皇上神化斂布徵積於持久士歲
punctuated: 視舊加倍矣。夫養士以專豫之教，則業守其常而志一；擇士以精慎之法，則官得其理而事勸。此我聖祖所以遺久安長治之道於無窮者。我皇上籲俊知宅，夙夜勤毖，故士斐然宣灼於實用，旁溢詞藝，不可以曩昔觀也。臣頃隸史署，嘗再預校士之末，已復司南考。今四入試闈，叨典事，讀士之文而推其志，察士之志而占其所從嚮，仰窺我皇上神化斂布，徵積於持久。士歲
translation_en:
…has doubled in comparison with former practice. When scholars are nurtured through focused, preparatory instruction, their studies follow a constant course and their aspirations become single-minded; when scholars are selected by exacting and careful procedures, offices are properly administered and diligence in service is encouraged. This is how our Sagely Founder bequeathed the means of lasting peace and enduring good government for all time. Our Emperor summons outstanding men and knows where to place them, working diligently and circumspectly day and night. Thus scholars shine brilliantly in practical service, their accomplishments extending also to literary composition; they cannot be viewed as scholars were in former times.

Your servant recently served in the historiographical office. I twice had the honor of taking a humble part in examining scholars, and subsequently presided over an examination in the south. Now, entering the examination compound for the fourth time and undeservedly entrusted with its affairs, I read the scholars’ compositions to infer their aspirations, and scrutinize their aspirations to discern the direction they will follow. Looking reverently upward, I glimpse how our Emperor’s wondrous transforming influence gathers and spreads, its proofs accumulating over time. The scholars, year by year…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
異而月不同非其宜然與臣
報塞無能敢不竊之為以人
事君之私慶茲多士進矣臣
願終有告者自古賢材欲出
而有行患不得時有其時而
可出矣患不得用今
聖人在上作新萬類多士所值蓋
===
千載不易遘之時也出當有
司之擇用盍亦思所為迄副
其成者耶夫上養之而士遺
自養是棄菑疇於不播者也
上擇之而士忘自擇是登惡
莠以自殖者也我
聖祖耕稼求穫之望爾多士曷對
alt_text:
異而月不同非其宜然與臣
報塞無能敢不竊之爲以人
事君之私慶兹多士進矣臣
願終有告者自古賢材欲出
而有行患不得時有其時而
可出矣患不得用今
===
聖人在上作新萬類多士所值盖
千載不易遘之時也出當有
司之擇用盡亦思所爲迒副
其成者耶夫上養之而士遺
自養是棄菑疇於不播者也
上擇之而士忘自擇是登惡
莠以自殖者也我
聖祖耕稼求穫之望爾多士曷對
punctuated: 異而月不同，非其宜然與？臣報塞無能，敢不竊之為以人事君之私慶？茲多士進矣，臣願終有告者：自古賢材欲出而有行，患不得時；有其時而可出矣，患不得用。今聖人在上，作新萬類，多士所值，蓋千載不易遘之時也。出當有司之擇用，盍亦思所為迄副其成者耶？夫上養之而士遺自養，是棄菑疇於不播者也；上擇之而士忘自擇，是登惡莠以自殖者也。我聖祖耕稼求穫之望，爾多士曷對
translation_en:
…differ, and are not the same from month to month—is this not as it should be? Your servant is incapable of repaying these favors; how could I not privately count this as cause for rejoicing in serving my ruler by bringing forward worthy men [?]? Now that these many scholars have advanced, your servant wishes to offer a final admonition. Since antiquity, worthy and talented men wishing to enter public service and put their purposes into practice have feared that they would not encounter the right time. Once the time has come and they can enter service, they fear that they will not be employed. Now the sage sovereign reigns above, renewing all things. The time these many scholars have encountered is one scarcely met with in a thousand years. As they come forward to be selected and employed by the responsible officials, should they not also consider what they must do ultimately to fulfill the intended achievement?

If the ruler nurtures scholars, yet they neglect to nurture themselves, this is like abandoning a cleared field without sowing it. If the ruler selects them, yet they forget to exercise discrimination themselves, this is like fostering harmful weeds to propagate them among their own crops. Our sagely founding emperor cultivated the fields in the hope of a harvest: how will you, the many scholars, respond…

title: 嘉靖三十五年會試錄
text:
答之矧當時與用會乃不能
以志行功業自表見翼輔
邦家景長之祚則士之失職人
將孰與芘賴哉臣荷受
皇上豫養深恩擇處近密之任盖
往官太學曾承乏養士愧瘝
曠無庸自稱茲上被
===
簡命則又謬膺擇士重託益懼負
任使不能裨補萬一且內訟自
養自擇之道未先履踐於身
將言而人莫或信也故願與
爾多士交勗以相成焉爾多
士其尚茂勵毋忽也哉
中順大夫詹事府少詹事兼

爾多士交勗以相成爲爾多
士其尚茂勵毋忽也哉
中順大夫詹事府少詹事兼
punctuated:
答之？矧當時與用會，乃不能以志行功業自表見，翼輔邦家景長之祚，則士之失職，人將孰與芘賴哉？臣荷受皇上豫養深恩，擇處近密之任，盖往官太學，曾承乏養士，愧瘝曠，無庸自稱。茲上被簡命，則又謬膺擇士重託，益懼負任使，不能裨補萬一。且內訟自養自擇之道，未先履踐於身，將言而人莫或信也。故願與爾多士交勗，以相成焉。爾多士其尚茂勵，毋忽也哉！
中順大夫、詹事府少詹事兼
translation_en:
…answer that expectation? Moreover, when the occasion coincides with the opportunity to serve, if you cannot distinguish yourselves through your aspirations, conduct, and achievements, and help sustain the dynasty’s great and enduring blessings, then you scholars will have failed in your duty. On whom, then, can the people depend for protection?
I, your servant, have received His Majesty’s profound kindness in nurturing me beforehand and selecting me for a position close to his person and confidence. Earlier, while serving at the Imperial University, I provisionally undertook the cultivation of scholars; ashamed of my neglect of duty, I have no accomplishments to claim. Now, having received this imperial appointment, I have again been undeservedly entrusted with the weighty responsibility of selecting scholars. All the more do I fear failing this commission and being unable to contribute even the slightest assistance. Moreover, I reproach myself inwardly for not first having put into personal practice the principles of cultivating oneself and choosing one’s own course. If I speak, perhaps no one will believe me. Thus I wish to join you scholars in mutual encouragement, so that we may help one another attain fulfillment. You scholars should strive with vigor and never be neglectful!
Grand Master of Central Accord, Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently …
